key: Q = the question. Answers are separated into three columns: what we know with a source, what we still need, and what would resolve it without manual input.

questions.q: May this research be published at all, in this form?
questions.known: NFL.com terms 1.3 allow individual non-commercial informational use and prohibit systematic retrieval to build a collection without written consent.
questions.missing: Whether a frozen, attributed, non-commercial research note is acceptable, and what consent would be needed for anything larger.
questions.resolves_if: Written permission is obtained, or the source is replaced with one whose terms permit redistribution.
questions.owner_needed: No, but a rights decision is required from whoever publishes it.

questions.q: Are the originated Week 10 numbers internally consistent and reproducible?
questions.known: Yes in the narrow sense: one score pair per game drives both the spread and the total, and the build is byte-identical from hashed inputs.
questions.missing: Any external check. A coherent number can still be a wrong number.
questions.resolves_if: The originated numbers are compared with recorded market prices (S01).
questions.blocks: Nothing on the site; blocks every accuracy claim

questions.q: Is a 2.0-point home adjustment defensible for all 14 games?
questions.known: It is disclosed as a project assumption. No official NFL home-field value was retrieved.
questions.missing: A sourced home-field estimate, and separate handling for the Munich international fixture.
questions.resolves_if: A range is published per game (S08) and the neutral-site game is relabelled.

questions.q: Do we know which clubs are starting second- or third-string players?
questions.known: Two Commanders players are listed Out with a stated reason, and one Giant is Questionable with a reason. Practice participation is published for all 20 listed players.
questions.missing: Whether any of them is a starter, who replaces them, and how much the replacement plays.
questions.resolves_if: A depth chart plus snap counts are stored (S02).

questions.q: What does a blank game status mean?
questions.known: It is blank on the official page for 17 of the 20 listed players. The policy says a player certain to play is not listed on the game status report.
questions.missing: The page does not state, per row, that blank equals available.
questions.resolves_if: The league policy page is read in full and a dated rule is stored, or the field stays blank forever (S07).

questions.q: How much do two legs of the same game move together?
questions.known: Nothing measured. Team-level correlations exist but are a different quantity and five of ten are arithmetic artefacts.
questions.missing: Joint hit rates on the actual leg pairs.
questions.resolves_if: Paired leg outcomes are collected and phi with an interval is computed per pair (S03).

questions.q: Can three or more legs be priced from pairwise numbers?
questions.known: No. Pairwise dependence does not identify a joint distribution of three or more variables.
questions.missing: A joint model, or a simulation with an explicit and tested dependence structure.
questions.resolves_if: A copula or block-bootstrap simulation is specified, published and tested against outcomes.

questions.q: Is anything here skill-based rather than luck?
questions.known: Points-based expectation scored Brier 0.1575 against 0.25 for a flat guess on 32 clubs, so the scoring profile carried information about the displayed record.
questions.missing: Out-of-sample evidence. The comparison is inside one snapshot and cannot separate skill from a correlated season.
questions.resolves_if: Walk-forward scoring across two prior seasons (S04) shows the same result after the model sees only earlier games.

questions.q: How much of each club's record is luck?
questions.known: Every club is within about 2.2 wins of its points-based expectation; Denver and Tampa Bay are the largest gaps at about 2.17 wins.
questions.missing: Schedule strength, opponent adjustment, and any measure of how much of the gap persists.
questions.resolves_if: Opponent-adjusted ratings are computed from two seasons of dated results (S04).

questions.known: No. Zero strategies are qualified, no price was retrieved, and ROI and CLV are blank by rule.
questions.missing: Every price, limit, hold and settlement rule.
questions.resolves_if: S01 and S05 are completed and a forward record exists.

questions.q: What would make a reward decision reasonable?
questions.known: The blocked list is published: a dated price, depth and snap data, and a dependence estimate.
questions.missing: A forward, stake-capped record scored after settlement.
questions.resolves_if: The shadow ledger accumulates entries and the gate contract is met with artifact URLs.

questions.q: How much confidence does a single official page support?
questions.known: Each value is parsed from saved page text and arithmetic is re-derived; the extractor refuses to publish contradictions.
questions.missing: A second independent source for any value used in a decision.
questions.resolves_if: A two-source rule is applied (S10) and single-source values stay labelled.

questions.q: What did we choose not to transcribe, and why?
questions.known: Division and conference records, last-ten and several middle standings columns: the rendered table had no header row and its field order contradicts the page legend.
questions.missing: A reliable column identification for those fields.
questions.resolves_if: A source with an explicit header is retrieved, or the values are confirmed another way.

questions.q: Should the NBA material stay on the site?
questions.known: It is a completed, separately scoped audit and its own source terms still apply.
questions.missing: A decision on whether the owner wants one sport or a multi-sport workspace.
questions.resolves_if: The owner states a preference; until then the NFL section is the landing page and the NBA pages remain reachable and labelled.
questions.owner_needed: Yes, this is the one genuine preference question.
